2013}}</ref>

==High school==
===Playing career===
Mitchell played three years of prep basketball.<ref name=USAB/> For his career, he posted over 1,500 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 700 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]].<ref name=USAB/> As a [[senior (education)|senior]] at [[L. G. Pinkston High School]] he averaged 20.5 points, 13.2 rebounds, 4.4 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 4.1 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] per game while leading his school to a 26–10 record and a berth in the Class 4A Region II Tournament.<ref name=UNT>{{cite web| title =Tony Mitchell – North Texas Mean Green | work =MeanGreenSports.com | publisher =[[University of North Texas]] | year=2012| url =http://www.meangreensports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=9109&SPID=564&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=1800&ATCLID=205320061&Q_SEASON=2012| accessdate = February 8, 2013}}</ref> In one playoff game against [[Lincoln High School (Dallas)|Lincoln High School]] he recorded 25 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win.<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell was ranked as the #12 overall senior recruit in the class of 2010 by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name=UNT/><ref name=SI/> His accolades also included being named the 2010 ''[[Dallas Morning News]]'' Player of the Year – beating out [[Perry Jones III]], a future first round NBA Draft pick out of [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]]; a ''[[SLAM Magazine]]'' All-American; Texas' 12-4A Player of the Year; Texas Class 4A All-State selection; and being chosen to the Texas Association of Basketball Coaches All-Star Team.<ref name=USAB/><ref name=UNT/>

===NCAA eligibility issues===
Mitchell attended a public high school in Dallas for his [[freshman]] and sophomore years, but under the advice of his [[Amateur Athletic Union]] basketball coach he transferred to Center of Life Christian Academy (CLCA) in Miami.<ref name=SI>{{cite web| last =Winn| first =Luke| title =Ex-Mizzou recruit Mitchell ready to make comeback at North Texas | work =[[Sports Illustrated]]| publisher =CNN/SI| date =July 21, 2011| url =http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/luke_winn/07/18/Tony.Mitchell/index.html| accessdate = February 8, 2013}}</ref> What he did not realize until the latter portion of his [[junior (education)|junior]] year there, however, was that CLCA was not an accredited prep school, and therefore only a fraction of his coursework counted toward [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] eligibility.<ref name=SI/> Mitchell transferred back home to Pinkston to finish his prep career.<ref name=SI/> To make up for lost time at CLCA, he attempted to take make-up classes at a faster rate than the school district allowed.<ref name=SI/> After an investigation into his course load, and upon discovering Mitchell's attempted expedition of his graduation requirements, his transcript got invalidated and his high school graduation was postponed while he struggled with Texas' exit test.<ref name=SI/>

Mitchell had already committed to play for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] while these issues unfolded.<ref name=SI/> Forced to stay at home in Dallas for the entire first semester of what would have been his freshman year playing for Missouri, it was not until the start of the second semester when he found out that he would never be allowed to suit up for the Tigers.<ref name=SI/> Mitchell then had to choose one of two routes: either play [[Junior college#Athletics|junior college]] basketball for two seasons, or play for a different four-year institution as a partial qualifier.<ref name=SI/> He chose to play as a partial qualifier for [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]], the local [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] school whose coach, [[Johnny Jones (basketball coach)|Johnny Jones]], had aggressively recruited him during his high school years.<ref name=SI/> 

==College==
===Freshman season===
He was selected by [[USA Basketball]] to the 12-man team to compete in the [[2011 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2011 FIBA U19 World Championships]] in Latvia from June 30 – July 10, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/oly/olybb/news/story?id=6696456|title=One prep player on U.S. U-19 team|accessdate=2011-06-26|date=2011-06-23|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> After sitting out the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11 season]] due to his eligibility issues, Mitchell officially began his collegiate career as a [[redshirt (sports)|redshirt]] freshman in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]].<ref name=UNT/><ref name=SI/> He quickly established himself as a premier player in both the Sun Belt Conference as well as nationally; Mitchell was named by [[CBS Sports]] as one of the "top 10 freshmen in the country" and their third-best "under the radar" player after averaging 14.7 points and 10.3 rebounds per game.<ref name=UNT/> Along with [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]'s [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]], he was one of only two freshmen in NCAA Division I to average a [[double-double]] (Davis was also that season's national player of the year and the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall draft pick]] in the [[2012 NBA Draft|ensuing NBA Draft]]).<ref name=UNT/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/|title=Draft Index|accessdate=February 10, 2013|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=basketball-reference.com|year=2012}}</ref> Among freshmen, only Davis' 10.4 rebounds per game average exceeded Mitchell's.<ref name=UNT/> He set school records for single season blocks (70) and blocks per game (3.04), while his single game top scoring and rebounding performances were 34 and 21, respectively.<ref name=UNT/> Despite the team not qualifying for any postseason tournaments, Mitchell still received awards and honors for his personal play. He became just the second player in league history to earn three consecutive Sun Belt Player of the Week awards while also becoming just the third player to be named the league's freshman of the year and earn a first team all-conference selection simultaneously.<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell was named to the All-[[2012 Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2012 Sun Belt Conference Tournament]] team after leading the Mean Green to the championship game before losing to [[2011–12 WKU Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]], 74 to 70.<ref name=UNT/> According to his North Texas player page, "In league-only games, Mitchell led the Sun Belt in scoring (15.9 ppg), rebounding (11.8 rpg), 3-point percentage (47.1), blocks (3.1 bpg), and was also second in field goal percentage (58.1)."<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell had numerous 30-point, 15-rebound games during the season and became the first freshman since [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]'s [[Michael Beasley]] in [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08]] to record multiple 30/15 games.<ref name=UNT/> For his standout season, he was named a finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], an annual college basketball award given to the nation's best [[mid-major]] player.<ref name=UNT/>

===Sophomore season===
Heading into his sophomore season in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]], national media had their eyes on Mitchell as a potential [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].<ref name=BR>{{cite web| last =Henry| first =Scott| title =Why Is North Texas' Tony Mitchell Not Playing Like an All-American?| publisher =Bleacher Report| date =December 24, 2012| url =http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1455713-why-is-north-texas-tony-mitchell-not-playing-like-an-all-american| accessdate = February 8, 2013}}</ref> He had been a projected first round draft pick in the [[2012 NBA Draft]] following his freshman season,<ref name=USAT>{{cite web| last =Gleeson| first =Scott M.| title =Mid-Major Player Diary: Tony Mitchell doesn't regret NBA decision| publisher =''[[USA Today]]''| date =January 8, 2013| url =http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/01/08/mid-major-player-diary-tony-mitchell-doesnt-regret-nba-decision/1793449/| accessdate = February 8, 2013}}</ref> but opted to remain at North Texas because he said he "still needed to mature on and off the court."<ref name=USAT/> Some of the preseason watchlists and honors that Mitchell received included being an All-American according to numerous media outlets; a [[John Wooden Award]] Preseason Top 50 player; being featured on the October cover of ''[[Basketball Times]]''; Lindy's number two ranked [[center (basketball)|center]] in college basketball; and CBS Sports' number seven overall player in the country.<ref name=UNT/> He was listed as a "near guarantee" to be named the 2013 [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Player of the Year]] according to CBS Sports.<ref name=PREVIEW/> An anonymous Sun Belt coach said of Mitchell: "[He] is the most athletic guy in college basketball, bar none. Rebounds as good as anyone. He's a freak."<ref name=PREVIEW/>

Mitchell's per-game averages lowered in four of the five major statistical categories from his freshman season: 13.0 points (down from 14.7), 8.5 rebounds (down from 10.3), 0.8 assists (down from 1.6), and 2.7 blocks (down from 3.0).<ref name=SR>{{cite web|title =Tony Mitchell| publisher =Sports Reference LLC| work=sports-reference.com | date =February 11, 2013| url =http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tony-mitchell-4.html| accessdate = February 11, 2013}}</ref> Only his steals per game average increased, going from 0.9 as a freshman to 1.0 in his second year.<ref name=SR/> Additionally, the North Texas squad managed just a 12–20 overall record (7–13 in conference) after being selected as the preseason Sun Belt Conference champions.<ref>{{cite web|title =2012–13 North Texas results| publisher =University of North Texas| work=MeanGreenSports.com | date =February 11, 2013| url =http://www.meangreensports.com/SportSelect.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=1800&SPID=564&SPSID=9108| accessdate = February 11, 2013}}</ref> Midway through the season, [[Bleacher Report]] wrote an article which said that questioned Mitchell's ability to lead a team since a talent of his caliber should have been a bigger factor in games played in a mid-major conference.<ref name=BR/> The article also said that his All-American candidacy took a severe blow, and that his per game averages would be more impressive if he played for a stronger Division I program.<ref name=BR/>

==Professional==
With a college postseason invitation not occurring, Mitchell decided to be the first underclassman to declare for the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. He would also be the first North Texas player to be drafted in the NBA since the [[Dallas Mavericks]] drafted John Horrocks in [[1984 NBA Draft|1984]].<ref name=UNTDRAFT>{{cite web|title =North Texas NBA Draft Picks| publisher =Mean Green Ball | year=2013| url =http://meangreenball.com/north-texas-basketball/roster_nba_draft| accessdate = March 27, 2013}}</ref> In addition, he is projected to be drafted in the first round, which would make him the first ever basketball player to spend their entire college career with North Texas to do so.<ref name=UNTDRAFT/>

==Personal==
Mitchell was born in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]] but grew up in Dallas.<ref name=USAB/> His parents are Angie L. Mitchell and Tony L. Mitchell, Sr., and he has a younger brother, Antonio.<ref name=USAB/>
